paragraphs: Learning from incorrect labels often depends on estimating how true classes become corrupted. A noise transition matrix records those probabilities and helps a classifier account for labeling mistakes. Existing approaches rely on anchor points: examples that belong to one class with near certainty. When those examples are unavailable, estimating the matrix becomes harder and classification can deteriorate.

The paper proposes T-Revision, which replaces dependence on exact anchors with an initial estimate followed by a learned correction. It first uses examples with high predicted probabilities for their observed, potentially noisy classes. These provide an anchor-like starting point. It then adds an adjustable correction to the matrix and learns and validates that correction together with the classifier using noisy data.

Experiments on simulated benchmark noise and real-world noisy labels show better performance than the compared state-of-the-art methods without exact anchor points. The contribution is therefore an empirically supported way to revise an imperfect noise model alongside classification, rather than treating the initial transition estimate as fixed.
neurips-2019-are-anchor-points-really-in.tldr: T-Revision learns and corrects a label-noise transition matrix without requiring exact anchor points, improving classification in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: When several related datasets describe networks of relationships, estimating their graphs together can reveal structure they share. At the same time, the strength of a relationship may differ across datasets. This paper addresses both goals: learning a common pattern of sparse connections while allowing the corresponding precision matrices to vary.

The proposed Bayesian method uses group regularization built from spike-and-slab Lasso priors. These priors support distinguishing connections that should be suppressed from those that should remain. Applying this idea jointly across graphical models encourages shared sparsity without forcing every model to have identical numerical parameters. The distinction matters because common connectivity can coexist with heterogeneous relationship strengths.

The theoretical results establish an optimal convergence rate in the maximum-entry error norm and strong guarantees for recovering graph structure, including when signal strengths differ across graphs. Simulations and an application to capital bike-sharing network data show competitive performance against existing alternatives. Together, these findings support joint estimation that shares structural information while preserving differences among the networks.
neurips-2019-bayesian-joint-estimation-o.tldr: A Bayesian method jointly estimates related graphs, sharing sparse structure while allowing connection strengths to differ.

paragraphs: Voice conversion changes the apparent speaker in a recording. Training such a system becomes particularly challenging when the available recordings are non-parallel, meaning they do not provide matched utterances across speakers. This paper introduces Blow, an end-to-end model that performs conversion directly on raw audio under that training setup.

Blow uses a single-scale normalizing flow with hypernetwork conditioning. The conditioning mechanism lets speaker information influence the model through a speaker identifier. Training operates frame by frame, and the same framework supports many-to-many conversion across speakers. These choices bring raw-audio modeling and speaker-controlled conversion into one trainable system without requiring parallel recordings.

The reported comparisons find equal or better performance than existing flow architectures and other competitive baselines in both objective measurements and subjective evaluations. An ablation study examines the contribution of the main components. The authors also investigate training-data requirements and whether converted speech favors source or target speaker characteristics, giving the evaluation a focus on both conversion quality and the behavior of the model.
neurips-2019-blow-a-single-scale-hyperco.tldr: Blow performs many-to-many voice conversion directly on raw audio using non-parallel recordings and speaker-conditioned normalizing flows.

paragraphs: Behavioral cloning teaches an agent to predict an expert's actions from observations. This turns imitation into supervised learning, but the predictor does not automatically distinguish causal relationships from correlations. The paper argues that this distinction becomes especially consequential when the agent's own behavior changes the observations it encounters.

The authors identify causal misidentification: a learner can use the wrong observed variables to explain expert behavior. Because imitation involves a shift between training and deployment distributions, those relationships can become unreliable. One striking consequence is that giving the learner more information can worsen its performance. Additional observations create more opportunities to rely on misleading associations.

The proposed solution uses targeted interventions, through interaction with the environment or questions to the expert, to identify the correct causal model. The paper demonstrates the problem in benchmark control tasks and realistic driving settings, then evaluates the intervention-based solution against DAgger and other comparisons. Its central message is that resolving causal ambiguity can be an essential part of learning to imitate.
neurips-2019-causal-confusion-in-imitati.tldr: Imitation learners can perform worse with more information when they confuse correlation with causation; targeted interventions help resolve that confusion.

paragraphs: A neural network may behave differently at many locations along a single input line segment. Checking a finite collection of points leaves the behavior between them unresolved. ExactLine addresses this problem for piecewise-linear networks by constructing an exact, compact description of their output over the entire segment.

The method divides the segment into pieces on which the network is affine: within each piece, its output follows a linear transformation plus an offset. The algorithm supports common layers including ReLU, MaxPool, convolution, fully connected layers, and batch normalization. This makes a continuous set of infinitely many inputs accessible through a finite representation.

The applications show why that exactness matters. ExactLine identifies decision boundaries in an ACAS Xu network and computes integrated gradients exactly. In the reported attribution comparisons, earlier heuristics had relative errors of 25–45%; a better sampling strategy improved accuracy with less computation. The method also empirically falsifies the central assumption of a hypothesis about adversarial examples and reveals properties of adversarially trained networks.
neurips-2019-computing-linear-restrictio.tldr: ExactLine exactly describes a piecewise-linear network along an input segment, supporting precise boundary analysis and feature attribution.

paragraphs: Online learning studies decisions made sequentially as feedback arrives. Some settings reveal full information, while others reveal only part of what would be useful for choosing the next action. Researchers analyze these problems using several mathematical approaches, including information-theoretic arguments and optimization methods such as mirror descent.

This paper formalizes a connection between those approaches. Information-theoretic analysis combined with minimax duality has produced powerful guarantees, but its arguments often resemble classical mirror-descent analysis. The authors show that, in most applications, the information-theoretic bounds can be derived from existing techniques in online convex optimization. This explains a recurring similarity between analyses that otherwise appear to use different conceptual machinery.

The connection also accompanies improved regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with k choices, online linear optimization over lp balls, and bandits with graph feedback. Regret measures accumulated performance loss relative to a comparison strategy. The stated improvements therefore strengthen theoretical control of sequential decision quality across several feedback structures, while giving the analyses a more unified mathematical foundation.
neurips-2019-connections-between-mirror-.tldr: The paper connects information-theoretic online-learning analyses to mirror-descent techniques and improves regret guarantees in several decision settings.

paragraphs: A training curriculum changes which examples matter at different stages of learning. Starting with easier examples can help neural networks generalize, but deciding which examples to emphasize is itself difficult. This paper makes that decision learnable by attaching parameters to individual samples and to classes.

These data parameters govern each sample's and class's importance during training. At every iteration, gradient descent updates them alongside the network's ordinary parameters. The curriculum can therefore evolve as the model learns, without requiring manually designed scheduling rules. The approach treats the allocation of learning emphasis as part of the optimization problem.

The authors report consistent gains on image classification using CIFAR10, CIFAR100, WebVision, and ImageNet, and on object detection using KITTI, without increased model complexity or training time. On a noisy dataset, the method learns to favor clean images and reports a 14% improvement over state-of-the-art methods. These results support learned curricula at the scale of the evaluated classification and detection tasks, including a setting with unreliable training data.
neurips-2019-data-parameters-a-new-famil.tldr: Learnable sample and class parameters create a changing training curriculum that improves the reported vision results, including learning with noisy data.

paragraphs: Dimensionality reduction maps data into a smaller space while trying to preserve useful relationships. In metric settings, those relationships are expressed through distances. Practical evaluations often judge average distortion across the data, whereas much mathematical work has concentrated on the most severely distorted relationship. This paper develops theory around criteria closer to those used in applications.

The authors analyze several widely used average-case measures, including criteria associated with multidimensional scaling. They also study a newer distortion measure designed around properties desirable for machine learning. Beyond evaluating these criteria individually, they show that all the measures considered can be adapted to possess similar desirable qualities.

The main results are nearly tight bounds on the absolute values of the distortion criteria and approximation algorithms with provable guarantees. These contributions give practical measures a rigorous basis for reasoning about achievable embedding quality and algorithmic performance. The work's focus is the mathematical evaluation of dimensionality reduction, connecting commonly used quality measures to guarantees that worst-case analysis alone does not provide.
neurips-2019-dimensionality-reduction-th.tldr: The paper develops rigorous bounds and approximation guarantees for average-case distortion measures used to evaluate dimensionality reduction.

paragraphs: Hidden-role games require cooperation without knowing who is genuinely on the same side. This uncertainty adds a challenge beyond choosing strong actions against known opponents. The paper develops DeepRole for The Resistance: Avalon, where reasoning about other players' roles and partially observed behavior is central to effective play.

DeepRole combines counterfactual regret minimization with deep value networks trained through self-play. Deductive reasoning is incorporated into the regret-minimization procedure so the agent can reason about joint beliefs and infer partially observable actions. Constraints on the value networks produce interpretable representations of winning probabilities. Together, these components allow the approach to handle the full game.

Empirical game-theoretic evaluation shows that DeepRole outperforms the tested handcrafted and learned agents in five-player Avalon. The authors also evaluate it in online teams mixing humans and agents, where it outperforms human players in both cooperative and competitive roles. These findings demonstrate effective hidden-role play in the evaluated game, including situations where success depends on working with uncertain teammates.
neurips-2019-finding-friend-and-foe-in-m.tldr: DeepRole combines game-theoretic learning and deductive reasoning to cooperate and compete successfully in five-player Avalon.

paragraphs: Building a scene from partial observations requires deciding what might exist beyond what has been seen. This paper presents a method that constructs complete 2D or 3D scenes incrementally. Each addition remains globally consistent according to a learned scene prior, while accommodating both real observations and previously generated content.

The method models an active agent moving through a virtual scene. At each step, the agent either perceives an observed region or generates a plausible local completion. Such generated regions represent expectations about unseen surroundings. Because generation is statistical, the same observed evidence can support multiple imagined scenes rather than one fixed reconstruction.

The framework connects two endpoints: when real data is observed everywhere, it converges to solving simultaneous localization and mapping; when observations are absent, it can sample entirely imagined scenes from prior distributions. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness on several 2D and 3D datasets. The authors identify autonomous navigation and data generation for sample-limited applications as uses for this combination of observation, expectation, and incremental consistency.
neurips-2019-incremental-scene-synthesis.tldr: An incremental scene generator combines observations with varied plausible completions while maintaining consistency with a learned global scene model.

paragraphs: Training a graph convolutional network on every node at every layer can require substantial memory and computation. Sampling reduces that workload, but existing strategies introduce different problems. Sampling neighbors separately for each node can cause the required neighborhood to expand exponentially with depth. Sampling layers independently can leave too few useful connections between them.

LADIES makes sampling at one layer depend on the nodes already selected in the layer above. It restricts candidates to their neighbors and constructs a bipartite graph to calculate importance probabilities. It then samples a fixed number of nodes for the whole layer and repeats this process to build the computation graph.

This design combines a controlled layer size with explicit attention to connectivity across layers. The paper reports theoretical and experimental advantages over previous sampling approaches in both runtime and memory use. It also reports better generalization accuracy than full-batch GCN training, attributing that result to the method's stochastic nature. Sampling thus contributes to both training efficiency and predictive performance in the reported evaluation.
neurips-2019-layer-dependent-importance-.tldr: LADIES samples graph-network layers conditionally on one another to control computation while preserving useful connections.

paragraphs: Recurrent networks need a compact way to retain information over long periods. The Legendre Memory Unit derives that memory from a continuous-time mathematical representation. It uses d coupled differential equations whose state maps linearly to a sliding history window expressed through Legendre polynomials up to degree d minus one.

This construction organizes the history into orthogonal components, allowing relatively few state variables to represent extended temporal information. Training through the differential-equation solver also lets each layer adjust its internal time step and learn relevant time scales. The authors connect the results to learning scale-invariant features independently of the step size.

Reported results include better chaotic-series prediction than equally sized LSTMs, a two-order-of-magnitude increase in memory capacity, and reduced training and inference times. LMUs handle dependencies spanning 100,000 time steps and exceed prior RNN performance on permuted sequential MNIST. The paper also demonstrates an implementation using m recurrent Poisson spiking neurons, with linear time and memory costs and error scaling as d divided by the square root of m.
neurips-2019-legendre-memory-units-conti.tldr: Legendre Memory Units use a compact continuous-time representation of history to improve long-range memory and recurrent-network efficiency.

paragraphs: Linear approximate value iteration represents future rewards with relatively few parameters. Even when that representation can accurately express the optimal value function, repeated updates can fail. Combining least-squares projection with the Bellman operator may amplify errors until the estimates diverge. This paper studies that instability with access to a generative model.

The proposed algorithm builds value estimates by combining Q-values estimated at selected anchor states. Its aim is to preserve the compactness and generalization of linear models while obtaining the more controlled error behavior associated with interpolation. The anchors provide a set of reference estimates from which other states are represented.

The central guarantee has an explicit condition: every state's features must be a convex combination of anchor features. Under that condition, errors propagate linearly across iterations instead of exponentially, and sample complexity is polynomial in the horizon and number of anchors. Preliminary simulations on simple problems support the analysis, including cases where conventional least-squares value iteration diverges. The result identifies a sufficient geometric condition for more stable approximation.
neurips-2019-limiting-extrapolation-in-l.tldr: Anchor-based value approximation controls error propagation when every state's features are a convex combination of anchor features.

paragraphs: Training a neural network involves repeatedly adjusting its weights to reduce prediction error. Many improvements to this process change learning rates or add momentum. Lookahead introduces a complementary mechanism that uses another optimizer's sequence of updates to guide its own movement through the space of possible weights.

The algorithm maintains two sets of weights. One set consists of fast weights updated by an inner optimizer, such as SGD or Adam. Lookahead uses the trajectory of these fast weights to choose a search direction for the other set. Its contribution therefore concerns how a sequence of optimization steps informs a broader update, rather than requiring a replacement for the inner optimizer.

The authors show improved learning stability and lower variance for the inner optimizer, with negligible additional computation and memory. Experiments demonstrate that Lookahead can substantially improve SGD and Adam, even with default hyperparameters, on image classification, neural machine translation, and Penn Treebank tasks. These findings support its use as a lightweight addition to established training methods.
neurips-2019-lookahead-optimizer-k-steps.tldr: Lookahead uses two sets of weights to stabilize an existing optimizer and improve training with little added cost.

paragraphs: Collaborative filtering recommends items by learning relationships in users' preferences. This paper models dependencies among recommended items with a Gaussian Markov random field. The graph-based formulation makes item relationships central to the recommendation model and connects the task to estimating sparse inverse covariance matrices.

The approach uses an auto-normal parameterization and pseudo-likelihood to make learning computationally efficient. This formulation also links the probabilistic model to autoencoders and neighborhood models, both established approaches to collaborative filtering. The authors introduce an approximation for learning sparse fields that lets users control the balance between training time and recommendation accuracy.

Across three established datasets, the method achieves competitive ranking accuracy while using a small fraction of the training time of the compared methods, including deep nonlinear models. On the dataset with the most items, it reports a 20% accuracy gain. These findings indicate that the proposed dependency model can combine efficient fitting with strong recommendation rankings, particularly in the largest item collection examined.
neurips-2019-markov-random-fields-for-co.tldr: A sparse Gaussian graphical model delivers competitive recommendation accuracy with substantially shorter training in the reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Maximum mean discrepancy, or MMD, compares probability distributions through functions in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. When that function space is sufficiently rich, MMD serves as a genuine metric on distributions. This paper studies how a distribution can evolve to reduce MMD using a Wasserstein gradient flow.

The authors derive conditions under which this evolution converges to a global optimum. Those conditions matter because they specify when following the flow succeeds, rather than asserting unconditional convergence. The analysis can also be related to transporting particles during neural-network optimization, connecting an abstract evolution of probability measures to movement of a collection of representative points.

The paper additionally proposes regularizing the flow by injecting noise into its gradient, supported by both theory and experiments. Implementation benefits from simple closed-form expressions for MMD and its gradient, which can be estimated from samples. The contribution combines convergence analysis with a practical modification, making the distributional optimization process both mathematically examinable and straightforward to approximate computationally.
neurips-2019-maximum-mean-discrepancy-gr.tldr: The paper studies conditions for MMD gradient-flow convergence and proposes noise-based regularization supported by theory and experiments.

paragraphs: Complex bodies often need several skills to operate together. An agent that stores a separate primitive for every possible combination faces a rapidly growing collection of behaviors to learn. This paper proposes multiplicative compositional policies, or MCP, to learn reusable motor skills that can be combined for subsequent tasks.

MCP organizes an agent's skills into a collection of primitives and permits multiple primitives to be active simultaneously through multiplicative composition. The resulting flexibility allows learned components to be transferred and recombined when a new task demands a different behavior. This directly addresses the need for coordinated skills in high-dimensional characters such as humanoid bodies.

The demonstrations extract composable skills from pretraining tasks, including motion imitation, using complex simulated characters. Those skills are then reused for continuous-control tasks such as moving a soccer ball toward a goal and carrying an object to a target. The results show that the learned primitives support useful recombination in the evaluated tasks, giving hierarchical control a way to reuse experience across coordinated behaviors.
neurips-2019-mcp-learning-composable-hie.tldr: MCP learns motor primitives that can act together through multiplicative composition and transfer to new simulated control tasks.

paragraphs: Weak supervision combines imperfect labeling sources when expert annotations are expensive. Sequential data adds a complication: one source may label an individual element, while another labels an entire group of elements. Their errors and correlations must be estimated without labeled data, and the different resolutions make that estimation more difficult.

Dugong models these multi-resolution sources and their complex correlations to produce probabilistic training labels. Under mild conditions, the authors prove that the hidden accuracy and correlation parameters can be uniquely recovered. Parameter sharing improves sample complexity, addressing the difficulty of estimation as sequences grow longer. The recovery guarantee remains conditional on those stated conditions.

The method produces clinician-validated labels for population-scale biomedical video collections, helping exceed traditional supervision by 36.8 F1 points in that application. Across the evaluated video and sensor classification tasks, average gains are 16.0 F1 points over traditional supervision and 24.2 over existing weak-supervision methods. These results show how modeling supervision at several resolutions can make noisy sources more useful for training.
neurips-2019-multi-resolution-weak-super.tldr: Dugong combines correlated labeling sources at different sequence resolutions, with conditional recovery guarantees and substantial reported classification gains.

paragraphs: Sequence models often need to connect information located far apart in an input. Attention can serve this purpose, but its quadratic cost becomes expensive for long sequences. This paper introduces a Shuffle-Exchange network for sequence-to-sequence processing with logarithmic depth and total computational complexity proportional to n log n.

The architecture therefore offers a different scaling profile for modeling long-range dependencies. The authors test whether this more economical computation can still express demanding transformations. On algorithmic benchmarks, the model learns efficient procedures for sorting, addition, and multiplication, demonstrating that the architecture supports more than simple local sequence operations.

On the LAMBADA question-answering dataset, the network achieves accuracy competitive with attention-based models. It also scales to sequences containing more than 100,000 elements. These findings combine evidence of useful predictive performance with the ability to process very long inputs. The authors suggest language modeling, music generation, and other large interrelated datasets as potential application areas, presenting those broader uses as future possibilities.
neurips-2019-neural-shuffle-exchange-net.tldr: Shuffle-Exchange networks process sequences in O(n log n) time while achieving competitive language-task accuracy and handling over 100,000 elements.

paragraphs: Principal component regression reduces a large set of predictors to a smaller representation before fitting a linear response model. When predictors have low-dimensional structure, this can reduce the samples needed for accurate prediction. The paper asks whether that advantage survives when predictor entries are noisy, missing, or a mixture of discrete and continuous values.

The authors establish robustness in this setting. Writing r for the representation dimension, p for the original dimension, and rho for the observed fraction, they give a vanishing-error sample scaling of r times the maximum of the response-noise variance bound and rho to the minus fourth times log to the fifth of p. Thus the guarantee explicitly accounts for incomplete observations.

A key step shows equivalence between principal component regression and linear regression after hard singular value thresholding of the predictors. Stronger matrix-error guarantees make this connection useful for prediction analysis. The paper also derives generalization bounds that support selecting the number of components from data, connecting robustness theory to a central modeling decision.
neurips-2019-on-robustness-of-principal-.tldr: The paper proves robustness guarantees for principal component regression with noisy, missing, and mixed-valued predictors.

paragraphs: One-shot object detection asks a model to find objects matching a single example image patch. The queried class may never have appeared during training. The challenge is therefore to use the query itself to locate all instances of its class in a target image. This paper develops the CoAE framework for that task.

Its first component uses a non-local operation to identify relationships between the query and target image, producing region proposals suited to the query. A second component emphasizes correlated feature channels through squeeze-and-co-excitation. Together, these mechanisms guide both where the detector looks and which visual features receive emphasis.

A margin-based ranking loss then learns how to score the similarity between proposed regions and the query, covering classes seen or unseen during training. The resulting two-stage detector provides a strong baseline on VOC and MS-COCO under the evaluated one-shot settings. The contribution is a coordinated use of query-target interaction, feature emphasis, and similarity learning to make detection responsive to a single example.
neurips-2019-one-shot-object-detection-w.tldr: CoAE uses query-target attention, correlated feature emphasis, and similarity ranking to detect objects from one example, including unseen classes.

paragraphs: Low-rank approximation represents a matrix as a product of two smaller matrices while keeping reconstruction error small. The classical version can be solved efficiently. This paper studies a harder variant that adds weights and regularization, for which the general problem is NP-hard. The goal is to sharpen guarantees for algorithms solving that variant.

Earlier weighted approximation results provided polynomial-time algorithms when the target rank was constant. The new analysis instead expresses parameterized complexity through statistical dimension. This change allows a runtime guarantee independent of rank and can produce a significant speed advantage. The benefit is stated as a possibility arising from the different complexity parameter, rather than a universal improvement for every input.

The sharper guarantees come from stronger matrix concentration bounds, a new conditioning technique, and structural results about regularized low-rank problems. Together, these tools explain how regularization can support a more favorable analysis. The contribution is primarily algorithmic and theoretical: it identifies a way to characterize computational difficulty more finely than target rank alone.
neurips-2019-regularized-weighted-low-ra.tldr: Statistical-dimension bounds give regularized weighted low-rank approximation rank-independent runtime guarantees that can be substantially faster.

paragraphs: Deep networks can demand more storage and computation than resource-limited devices can comfortably provide. SCAN addresses this by organizing training and inference so that predictions can use features from different depths. Its design complements existing compression and acceleration methods, adding another way to manage the cost of a network.

The framework divides a network into sections along its depth and attaches shallow classifiers to intermediate features. Attention modules and knowledge distillation improve the accuracy of these classifiers. A threshold-controlled inference mechanism then makes processing specific to the individual sample, allowing the architecture to vary how it uses the available levels of computation.

Experiments report significant performance gains on CIFAR100 and ImageNet. The authors also report that SCAN can be applied to various networks without adjusting their hyperparameters or underlying architectures. These findings support a framework that equips existing models with useful intermediate predictions and scalable inference. The practical significance is the ability to make computation more responsive to a sample while strengthening the classifiers that enable that choice.
neurips-2019-scan-a-scalable-neural-netw.tldr: SCAN adds strengthened intermediate classifiers and threshold-controlled inference to make neural-network computation adapt to individual samples.

paragraphs: An auxiliary task can help a model learn features that improve its main task, but creating auxiliary labels often requires additional human effort. Meta AuXiliary Learning, or MAXL, learns those labels automatically from the available data. Its aim is to make auxiliary supervision useful without collecting further examples or annotations.

The method trains two interacting networks. A label-generation network produces auxiliary labels, while a multitask network learns the primary task together with the generated task. The label generator's loss incorporates the multitask network's loss. This creates a meta-learning interaction involving a double gradient, so auxiliary label generation is trained in relation to the learning process it supports.

Across seven image datasets, MAXL outperforms single-task learning without additional data. It also surpasses several alternative methods for generating auxiliary labels and is competitive with human-defined auxiliary labels. These findings support automatically learned auxiliary tasks as a way to improve generalization in the evaluated settings. The broader proposal is to automate part of task design that would otherwise require manual labeling decisions.
neurips-2019-self-supervised-generalisat.tldr: MAXL learns auxiliary labels through meta-learning and improves image-task generalization without additional training data.

paragraphs: Learning a graph from observations can help reveal relationships among variables, but a useful graph may also need a particular structure. Enforcing such structure directly leads to an NP-hard combinatorial problem. This paper develops a framework that represents structural requirements through spectral properties of the graph's Laplacian matrix.

For a set of important graph families, the authors show how to translate combinatorial restrictions into constraints on Laplacian eigenvalues. They combine those constraints with Gaussian graphical modeling to learn graphs from data. This creates a unified approach capable of handling a broad collection of graph families through a common mathematical representation.

The proposed algorithms have convergence guarantees and are presented as practical for tasks involving large datasets. Experiments on synthetic and real data demonstrate their effectiveness, with an accompanying R package supporting the experimental results. The key contribution is the translation from discrete graph structure to spectral constraints, which enables structured estimation within one framework. The stated convergence guarantees concern the algorithms; the abstract does not equate them with solving every structural problem globally.
neurips-2019-structured-graph-learning-v.tldr: The paper learns structured graphs by translating graph-family requirements into Laplacian eigenvalue constraints within Gaussian graphical modeling.
